title: Control Plane Core; MTQ Optional
canonicalChoice: MITHQAL is a neutral institutional settlement control plane; the MITHQAL Token (MTQ) is optional and disabled by default. The control plane is the canonical surface; MTQ is one possible settlement instrument among many.
reasonNotes: Reframing MITHQAL as a control plane rather than a token product removes the v25.x ambiguity about whether MITHQAL is a stablecoin, a CBDC, or a settlement network. Operators can use the control plane with or without MTQ; Pilot A never uses MTQ.
conditions: MTQ_ENABLED defaults to false in every environment
MTQ_PILOT_STAGE defaults to A in every environment
MITHQAL_PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZED defaults to false in every environment

title: PAR Accounting Reference
canonicalChoice: MITHQAL uses Pay-As-Resolved (PAR) accounting: every ledger entry is resolved to a final-state classification at commit time. No float buckets, no suspense accounts, no implicit reversal lanes.
reasonNotes: PAR was selected over accrual-basis and over dual-entry-suspense because it eliminates the 'pending state' that historically masked reconciliation gaps in v25.x. Every entry has a reason code at commit; reconciliation becomes a class-specific tolerance check, not a phase-of-flight heuristic.
conditions: All six reconciliation classes have an ACTIVE rule in RECONCILIATION_TOLERANCE_REGISTRY
Legacy 0.1% / 0.5% / 1% / 5% thresholds marked DEPRECATED

title: BM-15 Authorization; BM-16A Finality; BM-16B Mint
canonicalChoice: Three canonical BM module ids: BM-15 Monetary Authorization, BM-16A Finality Verification, BM-16B Mint Execution. BM-16B is disabledByDefault=true.
reasonNotes: v25.x used several inconsistent names ('BM-15-Mint', 'BM16', 'BM-16B-Mint'). v26.0 §4.4 locks the canonical names. getBmModule() throws on legacy names so callers must migrate.
conditions: BM-16B disabledByDefault=true
Legacy BM module names cause getBmModule to throw
canExecuteMint requires finalityState=F4 + stateSatisfied=true + MTQ gate ok=true

title: Direct-Matched Backing + Risk Buffer Separate
canonicalChoice: EligibleBacking = MIN(EconomicBacking, LegalBacking, LiquidBacking, SettlementAvailableBacking). Direct-matched backing covers the obligation in the same unit; the risk buffer is tracked separately and does NOT contribute to direct-match satisfaction.
reasonNotes: Replaces the v25.x '130% backing specification' aspiration. The MIN captures the institutional principle that no dimension can substitute for another; the separate risk buffer prevents the buffer from being commingled into backing eligibility.
conditions: CLAIM-LEGACY-RESERVE-130-PERCENT is CONTRADICTED in claim-registry-data.ts
Home page pillar wording replaced with 'Direct-matched backing (target, not legal rule)'

title: No Gold/Digital in Pilot 1
canonicalChoice: Pilot 1 (Pilot A) does not include gold-backed or digital-asset-backed instruments. The pilot scope is USD-denominated institutional settlement only.
reasonNotes: The v25.x pilot scope mixed USD, gold, and on-chain digital assets. v26.0 narrows Pilot A to USD only so that the reconciliation, evidence, and finality surface can be exercised end-to-end before adding asset-class complexity.
conditions: Pilot A scope document must be added
Asset-class enablement gate G-ASSET-CLASS must remain CLOSED

title: Neon Authoritative; Turso Projection
canonicalChoice: Neon Postgres is the single authoritative writer. Turso (libSQL) is the projection (eventually consistent, watermark-gated). There is exactly one writer per instruction; no dual-writes.
reasonNotes: v25.x experimented with both Neon and Turso as 'writers' and relied on application-level reconciliation to merge them. v26.0 §6.1 + §6.8 + Appendix B make the relationship authoritative: Neon writes, Turso reads from the OutboxEvent stream.
conditions: DATABASE_BACKEND=neon in production env
MITHQAL_AUTHORITATIVE_BACKEND=neon in production env
MITHQAL_PROJECTION_BACKEND=turso in production env

title: At-Least-Once + Idempotent Delivery
canonicalChoice: OutboxEvent delivery is at-least-once with consumer-side idempotency via InboxEvent + consumerDedupeKey. No at-most-once; no exactly-once claims.
reasonNotes: Exactly-once delivery across heterogeneous consumers (control plane, projection fans-out, reporting) is not provable. At-least-once with consumer idempotency is provable and matches institutional messaging practice (RTGS, SWIFT, FIX all use at-least-once + dedupe).
conditions: Every authoritative write is accompanied by an OutboxEvent in the same transaction
Every consumer MUST write an InboxEvent before processing
IdempotencyRecord conflicts surface as conflictingBodyHash mismatches

title: Atomicity Limited to Validated Common Finality Domain
canonicalChoice: Atomic operations are limited to the validated common finality domain (i.e. the F0..F7 path that has been policy-validated). Cross-domain atomicity is NOT promised; cross-jurisdictional atomicity is NOT promised.
reasonNotes: v25.x made implicit atomicity claims across the bank leg, the operator leg, and the receiving leg. v26.0 narrows atomicity to the F0..F4 operator-side domain (where we own the writer) and explicitly disclaims cross-domain atomicity in §4.2.
conditions: Operator-side atomicity is per-instruction (one OutboxEvent per write)
Cross-domain progression is gated by external-rail evidence at F6
F7 (legal settlement final) requires an EXECUTED_EXTERNAL_DOCUMENT

title: One Bank-Facing Counterparty
canonicalChoice: Pilot A has exactly one bank-facing counterparty. Multi-counterparty is deferred to Pilot B and beyond.
reasonNotes: Multi-counterparty settlement introduces reconciliation, netting, and tail-risk questions that the v25.x pipeline was not prepared to answer. Pilot A narrows to one bank counterparty so the F0..F7 surface and the bank-rail mapping reconciliation can be exercised end-to-end.
conditions: Counterparty onboarding evidence must be added
Multi-counterparty enablement gate G-MULTI-BANK must remain CLOSED

title: G0..G11 Critical Path; 20 Legacy Gates
canonicalChoice: v26.0 §9.1 defines the G0..G11 critical-path gate set. The 20-control mapping in §9.2 maps the legacy 20 gates onto the new 12 so historical audit references remain valid.
reasonNotes: v25.x had a 20-control grid that did not align with finality state boundaries. v26.0 §9.1 replaces it with 12 state-aligned gates (G0..G11); §9.2 preserves a 20-control legacy mapping for audit traceability without re-introducing the 20-gate decision surface.
conditions: G0..G11 each have a GateDecision row in production
Legacy 20 controls have a primaryGateMapping onto the new 12

title: CPI/ROI Require Measured Inputs
canonicalChoice: Cost-Payback Index (CPI) and Return-on-Investment (ROI) metrics require measured inputs (MEASURED claim status). Simulated inputs are not accepted for CPI/ROI attestation.
reasonNotes: v25.x accepted simulated CPI/ROI figures in marketing material. v26.0 §5.5 requires MEASURED inputs for any CPI/ROI figure that appears externally, and the External Claim Register enforces this via the isPublishable check.
conditions: No CPI/ROI claim with status SIMULATED may be published
Any CPI/ROI claim currently published must be re-attested to MEASURED

title: Production Authorization False by Default
canonicalChoice: MITHQAL_PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZED defaults to false in every environment. Promotion to true requires explicit operator action, a GateDecision row, and the G0..G11 gate ledger to be satisfied.
reasonNotes: v25.x had environments in which production-authorized behavior was inferred from the absence of an explicit flag. v26.0 §11.3 D-012 makes false the explicit default; the flag is treated as a credential that must be set deliberately.
conditions: MITHQAL_PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZED=false in default env
All endpoints surface productionAuthorized in their honestState field
Promotion to true requires a GateDecision row with decision=PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZED
